summary.oneLiner:
Karnataka Bank posted its highest-ever quarterly PAT (₹408.19cr, +40% QoQ / +62% YoY) and highest-ever FY PAT
(₹1,310.50cr, +3% YoY) in Q4FY26, delivering on nearly every FY26 guidance metric management had given a year
earlier (business, deposits, CASA%, GNPA, NNPA, ROA, CD ratio) under new MD Raghavendra Bhat (joined July 2025
after a prior-year "management crisis"), driven by a sharp NIM recovery (2.92%→3.07% QoQ), NPA/slippage
improvement and a steep sequential cost-to-income drop (58.72%→50.47% QoQ) — though management was evasive on
quantifying how much of the cost improvement and other-income jump was one-off (actuarial/yield-linked employee
cost swing, technical-write-off recoveries, Q4 seasonal card fees) versus structural.

financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | QoQ (Q3FY26) | YoY (Q4FY25) | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue (NII) | ₹843cr | +6% (₹792cr) | +8% (₹781cr*) | *mgmt worded YoY comparator oddly as "₹781cr" — likely Q4FY25 NII |
| NIM | 3.07% | vs 2.92% | vs 2.98% | FY26 full-year NIM 2.88% YoY; guidance was "3%+" |
| PAT (reported) | ₹408.19cr | +40% (₹290.79cr) | +62% (₹252.37cr) | Highest-ever quarterly PAT |
| PAT (FY26 full year) | ₹1,310.50cr | — | +3% (₹1,272.37cr FY25) | Highest-ever annual PAT |
| Gross advances | ₹83,339.92cr | +8% (₹77,283cr) | — | vs guidance ₹84,000–85,000cr — slight miss |
| Total business | ₹1,92,118cr | +5.12% (₹1,81,394cr) | — | vs guidance ₹1,92,000cr — met |
| Deposits | ₹1,08,778.75cr | +4% (₹1,04,112cr) | — | vs guidance ₹1,08,000cr — met |
| CASA (absolute) | ₹36,559cr | +11% (₹32,829cr) | — | CASA% 33.61% vs 31.53% Dec'25; guidance 32–32.5% — beat |
| Cost/income | 50.47% (Q4) / 56.34% (FY26) | vs 58.72% Q3 | vs 60.11% FY25 | Guidance 55–56% FY26 — slight miss on FY, strong Q4 beat |
| ROA | 1.27% (Q4) / 1.05% (FY26) | vs 0.92% Q3 | — | Guidance "1%+" — met |
| ROE | 12.69% (Q4) / 10.36% (FY26) | vs 9.06% Q3 | — | Guidance ~15% — missed |
| GNPA | 2.78% | vs 3.32% (-54bps) | vs 3.08% (-30bps) | Guidance <3% — beat |
| NNPA | 0.98% | vs 1.31% (-33bps) | vs 1.31% (-33bps) | Guidance <1% — beat |
| Cash / net debt | CRAR 20.07% (Tier1 18.68%, Tier2 1.39%) | vs 19.94% Dec'25 | — | LCR 165.34% (statutory 100%) vs 186.84% Dec'25 |
> **One-offs flagged (not fully quantified by mgmt on this call):** (1) Employee cost fell sharply QoQ/YoY —
> partly actuarial-revaluation linked to the yield uptick; CFO deferred exact split to post-call email. (2)
> Other income jump driven by Q4-seasonal ATM/card fees + recovery from the ~₹2,500cr technical-write-off book
> (~₹190cr booked in other income for the year) — treasury gain itself was only ~₹13cr. (3) PCR was raised 400bps
> in Q4 vs the ~100bps/quarter pace management had followed earlier — enabled by the yield-linked income upside.
> (4) Gross slippage fell to ₹147cr in Q4 vs a ₹250–300cr recent run-rate — flagged by an analyst as a positive
> surprise; management gave no specific one-off reason beyond "continuous recovery/monitoring effort."
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Overall business growth:** ~15% for FY27 (reaffirmed, "slow but steady, conservative").
- **Deposit growth:** 10–15%; **Advances growth:** 15–20%.
- **CASA:** maintain 33%+ of deposits.
- **CD ratio:** target 80% (was 76.61% in Q4FY26).
- **ROA:** "1% plus" (unchanged wording, no upgrade despite Q4 ROA of 1.27%).
- **Cost-to-income:** targeting 52–53% for FY27 (down from 56.34% FY26, 50.47% in Q4FY26 alone).
- **Employee expense:** expected broadly flat YoY vs FY26 (~₹1,500cr FY25-level referenced by an analyst) — no
  significant further reduction guided; management would not commit to a number.
- **NIM:** management believes NIM has "bottomed out" around current levels (~3%+); further improvement
  contingent on EBLR trajectory — no explicit numeric target beyond the existing "3%+" guidance.
- **PCR:** informal target of "+1% per quarter" continuing, though Q4 saw a 400bps jump; no fixed end-state % given.
- **Recovery from technically-written-off book (~₹2,500cr o/s):** management's stated (self-described
  "ambitious") aim is to recover ~50% of the NPA/technical-write-off book, but declined to give a year-specific number.
- **ECL transition:** estimated impact ~1–1.5% on net worth overall, phased over 4–5 years (~25–30bps/year credit-cost impact); capital adequacy (CRAR 20.07%) said to be sufficient to absorb it.
- **Branch expansion:** ~31 branches opened in FY26; FY27 plans intact but subject to "course correction" if
  geopolitical/macro conditions (Middle East conflict, oil prices) worsen — no firm branch-count guided.
order book & pipeline:
- Not applicable (bank) — pipeline proxy: ~₹2,000cr of sanctioned-but-undisbursed advances as of March'26
  (delayed disbursal), which management says "started happening post-April" (i.e., flows into Q1FY27).
- FY26 total disbursement ballpark: ~₹31,000–32,000cr (FY26 repayments of ~₹26,000cr + net advance growth of ~₹5,000cr, per MD's rough back-of-envelope answer).
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **RAM (Retail + Agri + MSME):** grew from ₹49,152cr (Dec'25) to ₹51,197cr (Mar'26); +4% QoQ in Q4. Housing,
  Agri, Gold and Vehicle loans together added ~₹1,547cr to Retail in the quarter.
- **Mid-corporate advances:** grew ~13% QoQ in Q4 — outpacing RAM growth; analyst flagged that 65% of FY26's
  incremental book growth came via corporate/mid-corporate, not retail/MSME (MSME "remained flat").
- **IBPC/Food-credit book:** deliberately run down from ₹4,057cr (Mar'25) to ₹1,707cr (Mar'26) — ~₹2,350cr
  replaced with higher-yielding loans during FY26 (low-yield corporate/treasury-arbitrage book being exited).
- **Retail term deposits:** ₹66,252cr (Dec'25) → ₹67,648cr (Mar'26), +2% QoQ / +5% YoY.
- **Bulk deposits:** down to 4.2% of total deposits (from 4.8% Dec'25) and 6.3% of term deposits (from 7.1%).
- No subsidiaries — standalone entity only.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Retail lending expansion:** Retail Credit Centres started October 2025 under new MD; retail growth
  "will not happen overnight" per MD — multi-quarter build-out still in progress.
- **Product pipeline (launches planned near-term):** Agri input loans for tobacco crop growers (tie-up with
  Tobacco Board, digital onboarding); Programmable CBDC (fund-use restriction to specified purpose/beneficiary);
  NFC-based QR "Tap and Pay"; surrogate-based lending for housing/mortgage; Dropline OD for MSME; LAP for MSME.
- **Technology/IT roadmap for FY27:** Loan Originating System revamp with collateral management, DevSecOps
  implementation, HRMS revamp, Treasury system revamp, BHIM 3.0 — also "exploring AI tools" for internal
  efficiency/process improvement (no vendor named).
6a. moat & competitive position:
- Skipped — no durable-moat evidence (cost position, switching costs, licence barriers, network effects)
  was specifically evidenced on this call beyond generic "strong customer-centric approach" commentary.
margins & cost dynamics:
- NIM 3.07% Q4FY26 vs 2.92% Q3FY26 vs 2.98% Q4FY25 — driven by RAM yield focus + CASA/retail-TD cost-of-funds
  optimization. Yield on advances 8.78% Q4FY26 vs 8.71% Q3FY26 (+7bps). Cost of funds 5.38% vs 5.46% Q3FY26
  (-8bps). FY26 full-year: yield on advances 8.94% vs guidance ~9% (marginal miss).
- Book mix disclosed under pressing from an analyst: base rate 0.31%, MCLR 5.59%, EBLR-linked-to-G-Sec 2.31%,
  EBLR-linked-to-T-bill ~55% (bulk of book), remainder legacy — no G-Sec-linked advances currently (a change
  from the earlier NIM-drag years when G-Sec-linked pricing lagged repo cuts).
- Employee cost fell sharply QoQ/YoY (below ₹300cr/quarter for first time in 13–14 quarters per an analyst) —
  management attributed to natural attrition/superannuation (~350–400/month retiring, replaced selectively) plus
  an unquantified actuarial-revaluation benefit tied to the yield move; declined to give FY27 employee-cost guidance.
- Cost-to-income improved sharply: Q4FY26 50.47% vs 58.72% Q3FY26; FY26 56.34% vs 60.11% FY25; FY27 target 52–53%.
capex / expansion (watch slippage):
- 31 branches opened in FY26. FY27 branch-expansion plans reaffirmed but explicitly caveated as subject to
  "course correction" if geopolitical (Middle East conflict) or macro conditions deteriorate — a soft guidance,
  worth checking next quarter for slippage.
capital allocation:
- CRAR 20.07% (Tier1 18.68%, Tier2 1.39%) vs 19.94% Dec'25 — ample headroom cited as reason bank chose to
  prioritize advances growth over further capital conservation this year.
- PCR (ex-technical-write-off) raised to 65.39% (from 61.23% Dec'25); incl. TWO 83.54% (from 80.90%) — accelerated
  provisioning pace (+400bps in Q4 vs typical ~100bps/quarter) explicitly funded by the yield-linked income upside.
- Good dividend paid in FY26 (referenced by a retail-investor caller; amount not restated on this call).
risks & watch-items:
- **New Executive Director hired externally** after the post ~9-10 months vacant; an analyst raised the
  cultural-fit risk given last year's friction with external hires — management deflected specifics ("past is
  history, present is reality").
- **ECL transition:** ~1–1.5% net-worth impact phased over 4–5 years, ~25–30bps/year credit-cost drag — confirm
  actual quarterly credit-cost trajectory once ECL rules bite (RBI timeline).
- **Corporate-heavy incremental growth mix:** 65% of FY26 incremental advances came from corporate/mid-corporate,
  not RAM — retail/MSME build-out is management's stated priority but has structurally lagged so far.
- **Employee-cost/actuarial volatility:** management explicitly would not commit to an FY27 number; the Q4
  step-down may partially reverse.
- **Geopolitical (Middle East conflict) exposure to NRI/FCNR deposits:** management says the book is "not
  sizable," low risk, but flagged as an external swing factor on branch-expansion pace and margins generally.
- **Slippage sustainability:** Q4's ₹147cr slippage (vs ₹250–300cr run-rate) — watch whether this holds or reverts.
management quality / tone:
- MD Raghavendra Bhat (joined July 2025, mid a stated "management crisis" year) repeatedly emphasizes a
  turnaround narrative: advances had fallen from ₹78,000cr to ₹71,000cr before recovering to ₹83,340cr; frames
  FY26 as delivering on "every" guided metric from a year ago. Confident, combative tone with skeptical
  analysts ("you are not believing me... we will do it").
- Notably evasive/deferred-to-email on several specific quantifications: gratuity/actuarial cost breakdown,
  G-Sec vs T-bill book split (initially), FY27 employee-cost number, exact PCR end-target — a pattern of strong
  qualitative reassurance without hard numeric commitments beyond the headline ratios already guided.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The "second consecutive quarter of growth" (per an analyst) is explicitly a recovery from a self-admitted
  weak FY25 (advances degrew from ₹78,000cr to ₹71,000cr) — YoY comparisons on advances (₹78,000cr→₹83,000cr)
  understate the actual turnaround magnitude (₹71,000cr→₹83,000cr) that management prefers to cite.
- Bank has intentionally exited low-yield, opportunistic corporate/treasury-arbitrage lending (IBPC/Food
  Credit book down ~58% YoY) in favor of RAM — a genuine mix-shift, not just a headline number.
- Growth is now explicitly phased monthly, not quarterly: management cited a granular monthly growth
  bifurcation (5%/8%/9%/10%/14% across the year) with H1:H2 split of 39%:61%, reflecting the bank's own
  10-year seasonality pattern (growth historically concentrated in H2/Q4).

identity.industry: Banking — Old Private Sector Bank (South India / Karnataka-origin, Mangaluru HQ)

hero.oneLiner:
Karnataka Bank posted its highest-ever quarterly PAT (₹408.19cr, +40% QoQ / +62% YoY) and highest-ever FY PAT
(₹1,310.50cr, +3% YoY) in Q4FY26, delivering on nearly every FY26 guidance metric management had given a year
earlier (business, deposits, CASA%, GNPA, NNPA, ROA, CD ratio) under new MD Raghavendra Bhat (joined July 2025
after a prior-year "management crisis"), driven by a sharp NIM recovery (2.92%→3.07% QoQ), NPA/slippage
improvement and a steep sequential cost-to-income drop (58.72%→50.47% QoQ) — though management was evasive on
quantifying how much of the cost improvement and other-income jump was one-off (actuarial/yield-linked employee
cost swing, technical-write-off recoveries, Q4 seasonal card fees) versus structural.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- "100+ Year Legacy" bank (CIN dates incorporation to 1924) branded "Banking with Legacy, Embracing the Future" and "Bharat Ka Karnataka Bank", with 14 Mn "Happy customers".
- Governance framed as a differentiator: "Guided by an Independent Board — With no Shareholder Holding >5% Share Capital in the Bank"; board includes former ED of Reserve Bank of India, former MD of State Bank of India (Part Time Chairman) and former MD of State Bank of Travancore.
- Stated strength areas: "Tradition with Innovation", "Outbound Sales Culture", "Startup-like Agility", "Capitalise on community network", "MSME and Rural to be key growth drivers", "Focus on Retail - Home, Gold Loans", "Wider Geographical Presence", "Digital and Data-driven client acquisition", "Cross Selling".
- Deck claims a 4% market share in Karnataka (footnoted "By share of Deposits as on Mar 2026") and 32.1% share of MSME & Agri-Loans.
- Management continuity is emphasised: MD & CEO with "38 years at Karnataka Bank", COO 35 years, CBO 30 years, CISO 30 years, CFO 25 years — described as "Strengthening of Management, making the Organization Future Ready".

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **RAM (Retail + Agri + MSME):** grew from ₹49,152cr (Dec'25) to ₹51,197cr (Mar'26); +4% QoQ in Q4. Housing,
  Agri, Gold and Vehicle loans together added ~₹1,547cr to Retail in the quarter.
- **Mid-corporate advances:** grew ~13% QoQ in Q4 — outpacing RAM growth; analyst flagged that 65% of FY26's
  incremental book growth came via corporate/mid-corporate, not retail/MSME (MSME "remained flat").
- **IBPC/Food-credit book:** deliberately run down from ₹4,057cr (Mar'25) to ₹1,707cr (Mar'26) — ~₹2,350cr
  replaced with higher-yielding loans during FY26 (low-yield corporate/treasury-arbitrage book being exited).
- **Retail term deposits:** ₹66,252cr (Dec'25) → ₹67,648cr (Mar'26), +2% QoQ / +5% YoY.
- **Bulk deposits:** down to 4.2% of total deposits (from 4.8% Dec'25) and 6.3% of term deposits (from 7.1%).
- No subsidiaries — standalone entity only.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body:
- Not applicable (bank) — pipeline proxy: ~₹2,000cr of sanctioned-but-undisbursed advances as of March'26
  (delayed disbursal), which management says "started happening post-April" (i.e., flows into Q1FY27).
- FY26 total disbursement ballpark: ~₹31,000–32,000cr (FY26 repayments of ~₹26,000cr + net advance growth of ~₹5,000cr, per MD's rough back-of-envelope answer).

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Overall business growth:** ~15% for FY27 (reaffirmed, "slow but steady, conservative").
- **Deposit growth:** 10–15%; **Advances growth:** 15–20%.
- **CASA:** maintain 33%+ of deposits.
- **CD ratio:** target 80% (was 76.61% in Q4FY26).
- **ROA:** "1% plus" (unchanged wording, no upgrade despite Q4 ROA of 1.27%).
- **Cost-to-income:** targeting 52–53% for FY27 (down from 56.34% FY26, 50.47% in Q4FY26 alone).
- **Employee expense:** expected broadly flat YoY vs FY26 (~₹1,500cr FY25-level referenced by an analyst) — no
  significant further reduction guided; management would not commit to a number.
- **NIM:** management believes NIM has "bottomed out" around current levels (~3%+); further improvement
  contingent on EBLR trajectory — no explicit numeric target beyond the existing "3%+" guidance.
- **PCR:** informal target of "+1% per quarter" continuing, though Q4 saw a 400bps jump; no fixed end-state % given.
- **Recovery from technically-written-off book (~₹2,500cr o/s):** management's stated (self-described
  "ambitious") aim is to recover ~50% of the NPA/technical-write-off book, but declined to give a year-specific number.
- **ECL transition:** estimated impact ~1–1.5% on net worth overall, phased over 4–5 years (~25–30bps/year credit-cost impact); capital adequacy (CRAR 20.07%) said to be sufficient to absorb it.
- **Branch expansion:** ~31 branches opened in FY26; FY27 plans intact but subject to "course correction" if
  geopolitical/macro conditions (Middle East conflict, oil prices) worsen — no firm branch-count guided.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Retail lending expansion:** Retail Credit Centres started October 2025 under new MD; retail growth
  "will not happen overnight" per MD — multi-quarter build-out still in progress.
- **Product pipeline (launches planned near-term):** Agri input loans for tobacco crop growers (tie-up with
  Tobacco Board, digital onboarding); Programmable CBDC (fund-use restriction to specified purpose/beneficiary);
  NFC-based QR "Tap and Pay"; surrogate-based lending for housing/mortgage; Dropline OD for MSME; LAP for MSME.
- **Technology/IT roadmap for FY27:** Loan Originating System revamp with collateral management, DevSecOps
  implementation, HRMS revamp, Treasury system revamp, BHIM 3.0 — also "exploring AI tools" for internal
  efficiency/process improvement (no vendor named).

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- NIM 3.07% Q4FY26 vs 2.92% Q3FY26 vs 2.98% Q4FY25 — driven by RAM yield focus + CASA/retail-TD cost-of-funds
  optimization. Yield on advances 8.78% Q4FY26 vs 8.71% Q3FY26 (+7bps). Cost of funds 5.38% vs 5.46% Q3FY26
  (-8bps). FY26 full-year: yield on advances 8.94% vs guidance ~9% (marginal miss).
- Book mix disclosed under pressing from an analyst: base rate 0.31%, MCLR 5.59%, EBLR-linked-to-G-Sec 2.31%,
  EBLR-linked-to-T-bill ~55% (bulk of book), remainder legacy — no G-Sec-linked advances currently (a change
  from the earlier NIM-drag years when G-Sec-linked pricing lagged repo cuts).
- Employee cost fell sharply QoQ/YoY (below ₹300cr/quarter for first time in 13–14 quarters per an analyst) —
  management attributed to natural attrition/superannuation (~350–400/month retiring, replaced selectively) plus
  an unquantified actuarial-revaluation benefit tied to the yield move; declined to give FY27 employee-cost guidance.
- Cost-to-income improved sharply: Q4FY26 50.47% vs 58.72% Q3FY26; FY26 56.34% vs 60.11% FY25; FY27 target 52–53%.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- CRAR 20.07% (Tier1 18.68%, Tier2 1.39%) vs 19.94% Dec'25 — ample headroom cited as reason bank chose to
  prioritize advances growth over further capital conservation this year.
- PCR (ex-technical-write-off) raised to 65.39% (from 61.23% Dec'25); incl. TWO 83.54% (from 80.90%) — accelerated
  provisioning pace (+400bps in Q4 vs typical ~100bps/quarter) explicitly funded by the yield-linked income upside.
- Good dividend paid in FY26 (referenced by a retail-investor caller; amount not restated on this call).

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **New Executive Director hired externally** after the post ~9-10 months vacant; an analyst raised the
  cultural-fit risk given last year's friction with external hires — management deflected specifics ("past is
  history, present is reality").
- **ECL transition:** ~1–1.5% net-worth impact phased over 4–5 years, ~25–30bps/year credit-cost drag — confirm
  actual quarterly credit-cost trajectory once ECL rules bite (RBI timeline).
- **Corporate-heavy incremental growth mix:** 65% of FY26 incremental advances came from corporate/mid-corporate,
  not RAM — retail/MSME build-out is management's stated priority but has structurally lagged so far.
- **Employee-cost/actuarial volatility:** management explicitly would not commit to an FY27 number; the Q4
  step-down may partially reverse.
- **Geopolitical (Middle East conflict) exposure to NRI/FCNR deposits:** management says the book is "not
  sizable," low risk, but flagged as an external swing factor on branch-expansion pace and margins generally.
- **Slippage sustainability:** Q4's ₹147cr slippage (vs ₹250–300cr run-rate) — watch whether this holds or reverts.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Restructured book] Standard restructured portfolio of INR 763 Cr. in Q1 FY2027 is 51.4% Housing, 36.3% Others, 9.8% MSME, 2.5% Agriculture; the deck notes "Approximately 53% of the restructured portfolio comprises loans that require a 30% recovery for upgradation", which the bank is targeting to move out of the restructured pool.
- [SMA disclosure] Special Mention Account book of INR 3,435 Cr. in Q1 FY2027 (vs INR 2,917 Cr. in Q4 FY2026) is attributed to "temporary aberrations", with the deck stating "Post quarter close, we have already regularized ~76% of these additions to SMA".
- [Awards] Two awards at "The Great Indian BFSI & Fintech Awards 2026" (Product Innovation of the year for Credit Line on UPI; Excellence in Distribution of Financial Products for Dairy Loan on ULI), an award for Best Product Customization in Finacle for Credit Line on UPI, and at the 5th IBA CISO Summit & Citations 2026 Winner - Cyber Resilience of the Year and Runner up - Cyber Security Team of the Year.
- [Cyber/regulatory] Enterprise transformation projects explicitly include I4C (cybercrime co-ordination) implementation and MNRL and FRI integration to combat cyber fraud.
